sample.title: 'Come all the way' back to EU, French finance minister tells UK | BBC News
sample.description:
Over 10 years since the EU referendum that saw the UK vote to leave the European Union, French finance minister Roland Lescure has invited Britain to "come all the way" back to the EU.
 
Hi comments come after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled a second Brexit referendum was "possible" in a future Labour election manifesto.
 
When asked about Burnham's comments, Lescure told the BBC: "British people decided, and that's obviously their 100% right, and if they're willing to come back, they will have to decide."
 
"But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime," he added.

sample.title: Judge orders botched execution evidence to be preserved | BBC News
sample.description:
A judge in the US state of Tennessee has ruled officials must preserve all evidence related to the failed execution of Christa Pike. 
 
Judge Myles ordered that "anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained," including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, like packaging, inserts, and labels.
 
She also advised the state to take "special care" not to misplace or accidentally delete any information that may be pertinent to the case.
 
Pike, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September.
 
Her Lawyer Randy Spivey says he was told Pike was brain dead on Monday, and it was expected that she would have her life support machine turned off on Tuesday, but instead she woke up and began speaking.
 
Pike remains in hospital, where she is receiving critical medical care and is being restrained at her hands and feet.

sample.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies aged 87 | BBC News
sample.description:
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.
 
Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford steep rent increases.
 
The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.
 
Announcing her death, Madrid Tenants' Union said Abascal's situation marked "a turning point in the history of this country".
